Reference written to [dsh-plugin-architecture.md]() (64 KB, 1177 lines). ## Summary **Minimum plugin `package.json`** (out-of-tree): ```json { "name": "dsh-hello-plugin", "version": "0.1.0", "type": "module", "main": "index.js", "files": ["index.js", "cordis.patch.yml"], "peerDependencies": { "@deepseek-ai/cordis": "^0.2", "@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools": "^0.2" }, "dsh": { "bundle": { "patch": "./cordis.patch.yml" } } } ``` In-repo packages add `types` → `lib/types/index.d.ts`, an `exports` map of `{types, default}` pairs plus `./src/*` and `./package.json`, `files` without `src`, and every `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` peer **mirrored in devDependencies** (cordis in both, same range — the plugin must share the host's single Cordis instance). `dsh.bundle.patch` — not a `cordis` key — is what marks a bundle; without it the package installs as a plain dependency and activates nothing. Subpath plugins are just an extra `exports` entry plus a second `name: '/subpath'` row. **Bundle declaration & install.** Declared by `package.json` `dsh.bundle.patch` (one path or an ordered array), whose content is a single `- insert:` list applied over the empty profile root. Installed via the `plugin_manager` `install_bundle` action or `dsh plugin --profile

add `: snapshot `package.json`+`pnpm-lock.yaml` → optional `git ls-remote` GitHub check → `pnpm add` (registry fallback loop) → diff deps to identify the one new name → require `dsh.bundle` or fail `not-bundle` → peer-compat check → eagerly parse every patch file → append to `dsh.profile.bundles` atomically → reload or `restart-required`. Only `$DSH_HOME/profiles//` is written; the user edits `cordis.patch.yml` there (or `$DSH_HOME/cordis.patch.yml`, which outranks it) to add rows. **Dynamic tool registration: YES.** The only unregister API is the disposer returned by `ctx.tools.register(definition): () => void` (`packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:1057-1088`), alongside `get(name, scope?)`, `schemas(scope?)`, `guard`, `restrict`, `presentAs`. Registration is a Cordis effect owned by the registering Context's fiber (`ScopedLayers.effect`, `packages/core/scope/src/store.ts:226-266`) — scope is global for a plain `ctx`, that agent's layer for `agent.ctx`, and teardown is automatic on fiber disposal. Shipped proof: `tool-bash/src/index.ts:536-554` re-registers as `ctx.jobs` appears/disappears. One limit: `ctx.effect()` throws `INACTIVE_EFFECT` after fiber disposal, so "runtime" means during the plugin's active lifetime. **Tests.** `pnpm run test` (unit) / `pnpm run test:coverage` (the CI gate, per-file 100%); one package with `pnpm vitest run packages///tests`. Boot on a real context with `new Context()` + `await ctx.plugin(plugin, config)` + `afterEach(() => ctx.fiber.dispose())`, using `mountAgentLoopTestDependencies(ctx)` for the standard service stack; product-visible plugins also need a real Loader composition test booting a test-only `cordis.yml`. Reference written to [dsh-skill-api.md](D:\DEV\dsh-model-as-tool\research\dsh-skill-api.md) (686 lines, 7 sections, every claim cited to file:line).

## Summary

**Service key:** `ctx.skills` — class `SkillRegistry` from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill`, bound via `super(ctx, 'skills')` (`packages/skill/skill/src/index.ts:374`). Only **five public methods** exist:

```ts
registerProvider(create: (control: SkillProviderControl) => SkillProvider): () => void  // :390
register(skill: SkillRegistration): () => void                                          // :439
async list(options: SkillViewOptions = {}): Promise<SkillSummary[]>                     // :470
async snapshot(options: SkillViewOptions = {}): Promise<SkillCatalogSnapshot>           // :481
async get(name: string, options: SkillViewOptions = {}): Promise<SkillDefinition | undefined>  // :500
```

No `unregister`/`remove`/`has`/`invalidate` on the service.

**Provider seam: yes, first-class.** `SkillProvider { readonly name; readonly list(options) => Promise<readonly SkillCandidate[] | SkillProviderObservation>; readonly get(candidate, options) => Promise<SkillDefinition|undefined> }` (`:247-267`); an array return is complete-discovery shorthand, `{candidates, complete:false}` is degraded-and-uncacheable. Factory gets `SkillProviderControl { signal, invalidate() }` (`:270-275`). Composition is layered: nearest scope layer wins a name outright, then within a layer `rank → providerOrder → localOrder` (project-dsh 100 … user-agents 500, runtime 250, bundled 600).

**Dependency declaration:** `export const inject = ['skills']`. The `declare module '@deepseek-ai/cordis' { interface Context { skills: SkillRegistry } }` augmentation is *published by the skill package itself* (`:283-298`) — an author only needs `import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill'`.

**Most important gotcha — the scoping asymmetry:** *writes infer scope from the calling context; reads require it explicitly.* `ctx.skills.register(...)` through a plain plugin context → global layer (all agents). Through `agentCtx` in `setup(agentCtx, agent)` → that agent's layer only. But `list/snapshot/get` **never infer**: omitting `options.scope` reads the global layer alone, so an agent-scoped skill is invisible unless you pass `scope: agent` (as the real `skill` tool does at `tool-skill/src/index.ts:133`).

Secondary: `candidate.provider` must equal `provider.name` or validation throws; `'runtime'` is reserved; same-name `register()` in one layer is first-wins-with-warning and returns a **no-op disposer**. Noted explicitly: no production in-repo caller of `register()` — all shipped skills are providers.
